name: Mike Wirth

career.title: Design engineer, then engineering, construction and operations roles
President, Marketing, Asia/Middle East/Africa (based in Singapore)
Executive Vice President, Midstream & Development; Vice Chairman from Feb. 2017

background_rationale: A chemical engineer who joined Chevron in 1982 as a design engineer and rose through engineering, operations, refining and downstream leadership to the top job.

notable.summary: Chevron's board waived the company's mandatory retirement age of 65 for Wirth, allowing him to remain CEO beyond 2025.
Announced that Chevron would move its headquarters from San Ramon, California, to Houston, with Wirth relocating before the end of 2024 and corporate functions moving over five years.
Completed the $53 billion acquisition of Hess after winning an arbitration against ExxonMobil over Hess's stake in Guyana's Stabroek Block, which had delayed the deal for over a year.
Announced plans to invest more than $7 billion through Venezuelan joint ventures to roughly double production there to about 600,000 barrels per day within five years.

personal_story.hook: Before running Chevron, Mike Wirth worked summer jobs making ashtrays at the Coors brewery, where his father was an executive.
personal_story.summary: Wirth was born in Los Alamos, New Mexico, where his father worked at the National Laboratory; the family later moved to Golden, Colorado, when his father took an executive role at Coors. He played football and basketball and credits his coaches with teaching him hard work, discipline and teamwork. His first jobs were summer work at the brewery, including making ashtrays, and he was struck by the loyalty his father earned by engaging with workers on the production line. After a chemical engineering degree from the University of Colorado, he joined Chevron in 1982 as a design engineer and spent the next 35 years inside the company before becoming CEO.
